機械警報器主要由金屬製成，包括鑄鐵或鋼製的外殼、銅或鋁製的穿孔圓盤、鋼製的軸承和: Mechanical sirens are made mainly of metal: a housing of cast iron or steel, a perforated disc of brass or aluminium, and steel bearings and drive wheels. The internal structure includes a metal plug valve that opens and closes the airflow. Electronic sirens use a plastic or metal housing containing an electronic chip, a loudspeaker and a circuit board. The rotating mechanism of some mechanical sirens uses rubber or plastic seals to keep it airtight. The whole construction is sturdy and hard-wearing, to withstand long use and every kind of weather.
警報器是產生噪音的警示裝置，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 412.21: The siren is a warning device that produces noise, Hornbostel–Sachs number 412.21. The mechanical type sounds as a stream of air is periodically cut off by a rotating disc or by concentric cylindrical slots, and the pneumatic type is a free aerophone; the electronic type synthesises a tone in a circuit and plays it through a loudspeaker. It was once used as a musical instrument, for example to drive organ pipes, and later was mostly used by civil defence, fire, ambulance and police crews at disasters, air raids or emergency call-outs; fixed and vehicle-mounted versions are also common in Europe.

警報器的音色以氣流被週期切斷所產生的音調為主：氣動型靠轉盤或轉筒遮斷定盤孔，形成: The timbre of a siren is essentially the tone produced as the airflow is cut off periodically: in the pneumatic type a rotating disc or drum covers the holes of a fixed disc, making alternating compression and rarefaction, and the pitch depends on the speed of rotation and the number of holes; no fixed range is given. A single row of holes gives one note, two rows can give two. Volume depends on the motor, the compressed air, the horn and the amplification circuit, and some models reach about 123 to 125 decibels. Compared with the electronic type, the pneumatic type's timbre changes with the mechanical speed and can produce a steady note, a fast warble, a slow wail, an alternation of high and low, and pulses; the electronic type synthesises the tone in a circuit and plays it through a loudspeaker.
警報器起源可追溯至1799年前，曾用作樂器並驅動風琴管。1819年改進並命名，以: The origins of the siren go back to before 1799; it was once used as an instrument and to drive organ pipes. It was improved and named in 1819, sounding by cutting the airflow with a rotating disc. Between 1877 and 1880 the concentric-cylinder mechanical siren was developed, and in 1887 one was installed in a Scottish lighthouse. After electricity became widespread it was driven by an electric motor, and fire sirens became common in the 1920s; the electronic siren appeared in 1965, and after the 1970s most fell out of use as pagers spread. During the Second World War British civil defence used a network of sirens to warn of air raids.
